name: Gaussian Process
summary: Fits a smooth trajectory to a field's Sentinel-2 series and gives its 95 % interval, which widens where clouds leave gaps.

reads.label: Imagery
reads.value: Sentinel-2 L2A scenes over the polygon. A date counts when at least 30 % of the polygon is clear, and of two orbits on one date the clearer is kept

reads.label: Bands
reads.value: B02, B03, B04 and B08 at 10 m, with NDVI and EVI per pixel: the median over the polygon's clear pixels on each date

reads.label: Series
reads.value: The six medians projected on three principal components, each fitted with a Gaussian process of a seasonal oscillator and a local term, with heavy-tailed noise

method.label: Covariance
method.value: Per principal component, a damped seasonal oscillator plus a local smooth term

method.label: Noise
method.value: Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom, by reweighting

method.label: Period
method.value: Scaled per field by the multiplier of highest evidence, from 0.6 to 1.5

method.label: Interval
method.value: NDVI rebuilt from the three components; mean ± t·√(a·latent + b·noise), with (a, b, ν) per region

evaluation.method: Coverage of the 95 % interval on 45-day blocks of observations held out from development fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná, with the scale chosen on the training fields and checked on the validation fields, all from another reading of the same Sentinel-2 scenes.
evaluation.source: TERRA signal and spectrum models, gp_series 0.1.0 calibration

limits: Every number was fitted on another reading of the same Sentinel-2 scenes, not on series read by TERRA itself; version 1.0.0 will be refitted on those.
Calibrated on fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná. Elsewhere it would use one scale fitted on the three regions together, which has not been checked outside them.
The trajectory is smooth: a harvest or another abrupt change shows up spread over weeks, not as a step.

picture.subject: a soybean-then-maize field in Mato Grosso, September 2020 to August 2021, read as TERRA reads it: observed NDVI in orange dots, the model's trajectory as a green line and its 95 % interval shaded. Drawn with an earlier fit, before the NDVI interval was calibrated
picture.author: João Leonardi. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2020–2021
